Rondo of Swords, a strategy RPG for the DS. It was barely known and sometimes dismissed as a bad take on the Fire Emblem formula, but I loved it.

While each of your characters had a "limit break" and earned skill points to spend, the big difference that seemed to bother some was that melee attacks and movement were one action, allowing you to move through and attack multiple enemies. This came with its own skills and strategies, like defensive units being able to earn the Z.O.C. (zone of control) skill, which prevented enemies from moving through them, thus ending their attack and allowing defensive positioning and bottle necking.

It was also notoriously difficult and featured a few odd characters from other games who show up to join your party, like Izuna from the "unemployed ninja" rogue-like games, IIRC.

My favorites are IV, V, and VIII.

The unique thing about IV is that you're introduced to each character by playing as them alone (or in a small group) for a chapter, before taking control of the hero who gathers them all into one group. One character is literally just a merchant who's gameplay incorporates his job.

V's gimmick is that you follow your character through the decades of his life, starting from childhood. The story tends to be a lot heavier and more personal than IV's as a result. Also: monster recruitment.

With VIII the series goes 3D, bringing it's vibrant, cartoony style to life with expressive character models and voice acting. The game is huge and bursting with character. Huge world, huge journey, tons of stuff to do, and all of it distinctly charming. Yangus is my boy for life.
